thread:
maria: Heads-up — CI evals for the new-opt bring-up show a weird metric spike that looks wrong. Runner logs look like metrics are getting merged across different promptsets. anyone seen metric namespace collisions in the harness before?
aj: yep, saw something similar a while back when batch ids got reused. can you paste the runner log snippet?
maria: sure — here's the relevant tail from the runner stdout:
```
[2025-06-03T14:21:10Z] emit_metric: name=accuracy value=0.87 metric_id=accuracy run_id=1738002469 promptset=ps_v2
[2025-06-03T14:21:11Z] emit_metric: name=accuracy value=0.45 metric_id=accuracy run_id=1738002469 promptset=ps_control
[2025-06-03T14:21:11Z] metrics_backend: series_key=metrics/accuracy points=2 tags=[]
[2025-06-03T14:21:12Z] metrics_backend: wrote series metrics/accuracy count=2 mean=0.66
```
The backend series ends up with no promptset tag which explains the blended number.
sanjay: ugh. that's because the emitter normalizes by metric_id only before pushing to the aggregator — we intentionally reduced cardinality recently. but for evals we need promptset-level breakdowns.
dmitri: yeah — cardinality tradeoff bit us. eval harness metrics must include run_id and promptset tags so dashboards and alerting don't merge unrelated series.
olivia: this also explains why the regression alert on the new-opt model triggered — dashboards are aggregated per-model and were seeing the blended accuracy. so CI was essentially lying to us.
eval-bot: Eval run 1738002469 completed: 3 checks failed -> flagged for triage. details: https://ci.redwood.example/runs/1738002469
maria: proposed quick patch: emit with explicit tags. example in python runner emitter:
```
# before
metrics_client.gauge(metric_id, value)
# after
metrics_client.gauge(metric_id, value, tags={"promptset_id": promptset.id, "run_id": run_id, "runner_uuid": runner.uuid})
```
This keeps series scoped for evals but still lets ops aggregate when they intentionally drop tags.
aj: also add a unit test that simulates two promptsets emitting the same metric_id and assert the backend receives two tagged series, not one. small integration test for the metrics shim.
sanjay: I can put up a PR today. plan: 1) change emitter to include tags for eval runs, 2) add unit+integration tests, 3) add a compatibility layer that preserves older zero-tag exports for non-eval workloads. PR #: 4021 (WIP).
dmitri: assigning to @sanjay. also let's retro-run the last 3 suspicious CI evals with the patched emitter to recompute baselines and determine if the regression was real. create a small job to replay logs through the patched metrics shim.
olivia: :thumbsup: can you also add a dashboard tweak — show a promptset breakdown toggle so we don't have to dig into raw series next time? small front-end change and a linked saved query on the eval dashboard.
ci-bot: CI: triggered rerun for pr-4021-eval-metric-tags — job 2734 started, watching.
maria: thanks team. i'll open an internal issue to track the replay and tagging rollout. tagging note: make tags opt-in via run config for now (evals opt-in by default).
aj: FYI, we should also add a short doc blurb in the eval harness README about metric tagging expectations (what level of cardinality is allowed, and how to request per-promptset metrics).
sanjay: yep adding that to the PR description. I'll ping #eng-ml when PR is ready for review.
maria: great — once PR lands i'll kick off the baseline recompute and update the regression report.
